spots.name: Seville Cathedral
spots.summary: The Cathedral of Saint Mary of the See, better known as Seville Cathedral, is a Catholic cathedral in Seville, Andalusia, Spain. It was registered in 1987 by UNESCO as a World Heritage Site, along with the adjoining Alcázar palace complex and the General Archive of the Indies.

spots.name: Alcázar of Seville
spots.summary: The Alcázar of Seville, officially called Royal Alcázar of Seville, is a historic royal palace in Seville, Spain and one of the official residences of the Spanish royal family.

spots.name: Giralda

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Giralda is the bell tower of Seville Cathedral in Seville, Spain. It was built as the minaret for the Great Mosque of Seville in al-Andalus, during the reign of the Almohad dynasty, with a Renaissance-style belfry added by the Catholics after the expulsion of the Muslims from the area.

spots.name: Plaza de España
spots.summary: The Plaza de España is a plaza in Maria Luisa Park in Seville, Spain. It was built in 1928 for the Ibero-American Exposition of 1929. It is a landmark example of Regionalism Architecture, mixing elements of the Baroque Revival, Renaissance Revival and Moorish Revival (Neo-Mudéjar) styles of Spanish architecture.

spots.name: Metropol Parasol
spots.summary: The Setas de Sevilla or Las Setas, initially titled Metropol Parasol, is a large, predominantly wood structure located at La Encarnación square in the old quarter of Seville, Spain.

spots.name: Torre del Oro

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: The Torre del Oro is a dodecagonal military watchtower in Seville, southern Spain. It was erected by the Almohad Caliphate in order to control access to Seville via the Guadalquivir river.

spots.name: General Archive of the Indies
spots.summary: The Archivo General de Indias, often simply called the Archive of the Indies, was created by Charles III and inaugurated in 1785. It is housed in the former merchant guild building in Seville, Spain, built in the late 16th century.

spots.name: Casa de Pilatos
spots.summary: La Casa de Pilatos is an Andalusian palace in Seville, Spain, which serves as the permanent residence of the Dukes of Medinaceli. It is an example of an Italian Renaissance building with Mudéjar elements and decorations. It is considered the prototype of the Andalusian palace.

spots.name: Tomb of Christopher Columbus
spots.summary: The Tomb of Christopher Columbus is located in the Seville Cathedral since 1899. Previously, it was located in Valladolid, the Monastery of the Cartuja de Sevilla, in Santo Domingo, and in Havana.

spots.name: Museum of Fine Arts of Seville

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Museum of Fine Arts of Seville is one of the main art galleries in Seville, Spain, with a collection of Spanish visual arts from the medieval period to the early 20th century.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Museum of Fine Arts of Seville

spots.name: Maestranza
spots.summary: The Plaza de Toros de la Real Maestranza de Caballería de Sevilla is a 12,000-capacity bullring in Seville, Spain. During the annual Seville Fair in Seville, it is the site of one of the most well-known bullfighting festivals in the world.

spots.name: Palacio de San Telmo

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Palace of San Telmo is a historic edifice in Seville, southern Spain, formerly the Universidad de Mareantes, now the seat of the presidency of the Andalusian Autonomous Government.

spots.name: Parque de María Luisa
spots.summary: The Parque de María Luisa is a public park that stretches along the Guadalquivir River in Seville, Spain. It is Seville's principal green area.

spots.name: Alamillo Bridge
spots.summary: The Alamillo Bridge is a structure in Seville, Andalucia (Spain), which spans the Canal de Alfonso XIII, allowing access to La Cartuja, a peninsula located between the canal and the Guadalquivir River.

spots.name: Capilla Real de la catedral de Sevilla

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.name: Isla Mágica
spots.summary: Isla Mágica is a theme park at the Isla de La Cartuja, in Seville, Andalusia in Spain. The park has six themed areas and a water park called Agua Mágica.

spots.name: Triumph Square
spots.summary: Triumph Square is a plaza in Seville, Spain. It is located at the center of a group of buildings declared a World Heritage Site in 1987: the General Archive of the Indies, the Alcázar of Seville, and Seville Cathedral.

spots.name: Puente de Isabel II
spots.summary: The Puente de Isabel II, Puente de Triana or Triana Bridge, is a metal arch bridge in Seville, Spain, that connects the Triana neighbourhood with the centre of the city. It crosses the Canal de Alfonso XIII, one of the arms of the River Guadalquivir that isolate Triana as an almost-island.

spots.name: Hospital de la Caridad

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Hospital de la Caridad is a Roman Catholic baroque charity hospital building near Plaza de toros de la Real Maestranza de Caballería de Sevilla in Spain.

spots.name: Palacio de las Dueñas
spots.summary: Palacio de las Dueñas is a palace in Seville, Spain, currently belonging to the House of Alba. It was built in the late 15th century in the Renaissance style with Gothic and Moorish influences. The palace is one of the major historic homes of great architectural and artistic heritage in the city.

spots.name: Church of San Salvador
spots.summary: The Church of San Salvador is a church in Seville, Spain. It is the second-largest church in Seville, after the city's cathedral.

spots.name: Avenida de la Constitución
spots.summary: Avenida de la Constitución is an important avenue in the Casco Antiguo district of Seville, Andalusia, Spain. It starts from the square known as Puerta de Jerez and reaches the Plaza Nueva, considered the center of the city and where the historic building of the Seville City Council is located.

spots.name: Torre de la Plata
spots.summary: The Torre de la Plata is an octagonal military tower in Andalusia, located in present-day Seville, southern Spain. It was constructed by the Almohad Caliphate.

spots.name: Archbishop's Palace

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Archbishop's Palace of Seville is a palace in Seville, Spain. It has served as the residence of bishops and archbishops of the episcopal sees and numerous nobleman and military figures to the present time.

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.name: Church of Saint Louis of France

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Church of Saint Louis of France, located in the historic district of Seville, Spain, represents an example of Baroque architecture in the 18th century. The church was designed by the architect Leonardo of Figueroa and constructed between 1699 and 1731 on behalf of the Jesuits.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Church of Saint Louis of France

spots.name: Plaza Nueva
spots.summary: Plaza Nueva is a public square in the city center of Seville, Spain, containing the Seville City Hall. The land which the plaza is built on was formerly part of the San Fernando convent from 1270 to 1840. The land was later acquired by the local government and converted into a public square.

spots.name: Monastery of Santa Maria de las Cuevas

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Monastery of Santa María de las Cuevas, also known as the Monastery of the Cartuja (Charterhouse), is a religious building on the Isla de La Cartuja in Seville, southern Spain. The Andalusian Contemporary Art Center (The Centro Andaluz de Arte Contemporáneo (CAAC)) is now located on this site.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Monastery of Santa Maria de las Cuevas

photo.author: The original uploader was Asterion at English Wikipedia.

spots.name: Royal Tobacco Factory
spots.summary: The Royal Tobacco Factory is an 18th-century stone building in Seville, southern Spain. Since the 1950s it has been the seat of the rectorate of the University of Seville.

spots.name: Hospital de los Venerables

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Hospital de los Venerables of Seville, Spain, is a baroque 17th-century building which served as a residence for priests. It currently houses the Velázquez Center, dedicated to the famous painter Diego Velázquez.

spots.name: Seville City Hall
spots.summary: The Seville City Hall is a Plateresque-style building in Plaza Nueva in Seville, currently housing the City Council of Seville.

spots.name: Plaza de América
spots.summary: The Plaza de América, located in the Parque de María Luisa, was built by architect Aníbal González for the Ibero-American exhibition of 1929.

spots.name: Archeological Museum of Seville

hours.note: Closed Mon, Sun

spots.summary: The Archeological Museum of Seville is a museum in Seville, southern Spain, housed in the Pabellón del Renacimiento, one of the pavilions designed by the architect Aníbal González. These pavilions at the Plaza de España were created for the Ibero-American Exposition of 1929.

spots.name: Plaza de la Encarnación
spots.summary: The Setas de Sevilla or Las Setas, initially titled Metropol Parasol, is a large, predominantly wood structure located at La Encarnación square in the old quarter of Seville, Spain.

spots.name: Plaza de San Francisco
spots.summary: Plaza de San Francisco is a square in the Casco Antiguo of Seville, Spain. The Ayuntamiento, known as Casa consistorial de Sevilla, built in the 16th century, runs along the entire western side of the square. On the other side of the City Hall is the Plaza Nueva.

spots.name: Monastery of San Isidoro del Campo

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Monastery of San Isidoro del Campo is a monastery located in Santiponce, Spain. It was declared Bien de Interés Cultural in 1872.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Monastery of San Isidoro del Campo

spots.name: Royal Shipyards of Seville
spots.summary: The Seville Shipyard is a medieval shipyard in the city of Seville that operated from the 13th to the 15th century. Composed of seventeen naves, the building was connected to the Guadalquivir River by a stretch of sand.

spots.name: Hospital de las Cinco Llagas
spots.summary: The Hospital de las Cinco Llagas in Seville, Spain is the current seat of the Parliament of Andalusia.

spots.name: Santa María Magdalena, Seville

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Santa María Magdalena is a Baroque church in Seville, southern Spain. It was built in 1691-1709 to a design of architect Leonardo de Figueroa.

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.name: Alameda de Hércules
spots.summary: The Alameda de Hércules , or simply La Alameda, is a garden square or mall in Seville, southern Spain. Built in 1574, it was originally a promenaded public garden, named after the eight rows of white poplar trees that fill its central part.

spots.name: Church of Santa Maria la Blanca

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Church of Santa María la Blanca is located in the San Bartolomé neighborhood of the district of Casco Antiguo in Seville. It was built in the 17th century. It is the headquarters of the Brotherhood of the Rosary of Our Lady of the Snows.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Church of Santa Maria la Blanca (Seville)

spots.name: Birth of a New Man
spots.summary: Birth of a New Man, popularly known as el huevo de Colón, is a monument in Seville, Spain. It is a work by Zurab Tsereteli, consisting of a colossal statue representing Christopher Columbus partially enfolded by an egg-like shell.

spots.name: Museum of Arts and Traditions of Sevilla

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Museum of Arts and Popular Customs of Seville is a museum in Seville, Andalusia, Spain, located in the María Luisa Park, across the Plaza de América from the Provincial Archeological Museum. The museum had 84,496 visitors in 2007.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Museum of Arts and Popular Customs of Seville

spots.name: Castle of San Jorge

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Castle of San Jorge was a medieval fortress built on the west bank of the Guadalquivir river in the Spanish city of Seville (Spain). It was also used as headquarters and prison for the Spanish Inquisition. It was demolished in the 19th century and made into a food market.
